notes.title: Beta: Physics, Attack Controls & AI Overhaul, Shield Blocking, Open Field Map
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

Combat improvements have been stacking up over the last 6 months, so we decided it was time for an update.

This one turned out rather massive; with a new map, a major physics overhaul, revamped attack controls, smarter AI, and a bunch of long-requested features that are finally starting to feel like what we’ve always envisioned.

⚔️ Combat & Controls

• 🛡️ Shield Blocking (WIP): Initial implementation of blocking with a rough shield animation set. Functional, but still needs refinement.
• 🖱️ Mouse-Driven Attacks: Attacks now scale with mouse drag speed, making them feel faster and more responsive. The old “trigger” feel is gone.
• 🎯 Improved Aiming: Upper body aiming has been reworked — thrusts and swings now land more reliably and track better.

🕴️ Physics & Movement

• 🤖 Physical Simulation Upgrade: Characters are more physically simulated than ever, with improved balance and reduced reliance on artificial forces. They behave more human-like, with muscles only stiffening up when needed.
• 🦶 Procedural Footsteps: Foot placement is now handled procedurally, with proper hip movement and smoother animation.
• ⚖️ Dynamic Balancing: Characters lean their upper bodies and use their arms naturally to recover balance when stumbling or shifting weight.
• 🏃‍♂️ Locomotion Overhaul: Full rewrite of character locomotion. We've moved away from motion matching for better responsiveness and performance.

🧠 AI

• 💢 Smarter, More Aggressive: Enemies now land hits more consistently and press the advantage. Facing spearmen is especially dangerous.
• 📏 Tactical Movement: AI keeps better striking distance, cuts you off, and surrounds you more effectively when outnumbered.
• ⚔️ Battle Line Behaviour: AI now holds formation, keeping allies to their sides and enemies in front.
• 🗺️ Command System (Early Prototype): You can now issue basic movement and formation orders. It’s early, but the foundation is in place.

🌾 Other Updates

• 🗺️ New Field Battle Map: Open terrain map added — great for staging skirmishes in a completely open space.
• ⚜️  Heraldry (First Pass): Basic heraldry generation added. It’s random for now but will evolve with more structure and meaning.
• 🧾 New Main Menu (WIP): The main menu’s gotten a little love.
• 🐞 Bugfixes & More: And many, many smaller changes and bugfixes.

🛠️ Installation

The build is now live on the [beta] branch.

Let us know how it plays — and happy ‘strifing!

notes.title: Melee Impacts Cam & Hotfixes 2024.11.v7

notes.title: Larger Battles & New Location
notes.content:
This update delivers smoother, more dynamic gameplay at scale! Now supporting larger battles with improved physics, and an early preview of an upcoming castle scene, there’s plenty to explore.

Check out the details below to see what's changed in the playtest!

What's New

Location Preview: Explore a work-in-progress castle location, get a first look at what locations in the game will look like.
Larger Battles: Engage in (chaotic) battles with up to 30 active characters (64 max).
Basic Followers: Spawn allies who follow and fight alongside you in Training & Castle locations.
 Post-Processing Settings: Customize visual effects to optimize performance or tweak visuals to your preference.
Character Stress Test: Test your rig’s limits with 50-100 characters (no physics). Share your results!


Improvements

Rendering, Animation, & Physics: Major upgrades allow smoother performance, enabling battles with around 30 characters without lag (max 64).
Combat Feel: Improved hit reactions and stronger arms when handling long weapons should improve combat feel.
Responsive Locomotion: Movement remains fluid and responsive even during collisions, and better traversal of rough terrain.
AI Group Behavior: AI behave better in groups, though beyond small skirmishes things turn to chaos (AI is still very WIP).


Fixes & Minor Changes

Combat Animation: Top down (NE -> SW) strikes are now more forceful
Bow Aiming Fix: Fix bug where shooting bow would always aim at the target's head, bouncing off helmets
Post-Processing: Adjusted for performance and to improve shadow depth.
Terrain details: Significantly increased grass rendering distance.
UI: Added new input icons
Other: Many more bugfixes and tweaks.

notes.title: Combat Playtest Locomotion Overhaul, Performance Upgrades & More
notes.content:
Hi all!

Build 2024.6.v9 is live now on the `Beta` branch!

This build mainly addresses some of the biggest issues with the last build - namely the character movement/locomotion. This was by far the point we got most critique on (and rightly so). We're curious to hear whether its improvement for this build makes a difference!

Much work also went into improving the game's scalability from a performance perspective, so in future we will be able to run many dozens of characters without issue. These performance improvements are largely under the hood but you will already be able to notice some tangible results in the game, but these are still limited as it's a work in progress. Now that we have a solid foundation for performance, it's a thing that we'll be regularly improving on so expect more impressive results soon!

What's New
- Characters now lean their bodies into the desired movement direction
- When imbalanced characters now drop their stance and lean their upper bodies for more stability
- Camera shake of several types adding more weight to certain actions like dodging. Configurable in `Settings/Camera`
- Added an animation for equipping helmets. Press `9` to unequip them
- Adaptive combat music - responds to the intensity of the action

Improved
- Locomotion *should* feel more responsive now, with direct feedback to your input
- Combat footwork should be snappier and more responsive to your input, with reworked animations
- Character spawning - this used to take almost a second per character and the game would freeze up. This is now sped up significantly, and done partly in the background with fewer frame drops
- Performance framework - we've laid the foundations for creating a game that can support many dozens of characters. More on this in future updates

Fixes & minor changes
- AIs now more naturally move their arm around in melee (they would jerk their arms into place as fast as was possible)
- Tweaked damage values so blunt damage is less effective through armour
- Thrusts should be easier to land requiring less force
- Arms are more stiff making hits and thrusts more robust on impact
- Added a couple of helmets to the training scene
- Reduced spawn rate of 2H weapons while they are WIP
- You can now more easily spawn multiple characters in formation
- Replaced the atmosphere system, the duel should now be more performant (but temporarily disabled dynamic weather effects)
- Pressing `PageDown` now spawns a party of 5 to where you're looking, instead of at a predetermined point
- Fixed a bug where unfocusing the game for extended periods of time while loading a game mode could make the game lock up
- Changed fixed framerate setting to only allow for 50 or 60FPS
- Reduced default physics rigidity by one tick to 4

We'll be posting one or more updates in the days to come, where we'll tackle the following features:

- Improved focus lockon camera
- 2H animation moveset
- Polearm animation moveset
- Blocking & parrying animations and mechanics
- Combat footwork animation polish

In the meantime we hope you enjoy the latest changes, and as usual we really appreciate your feedback!

notes.title: Combat Playtest Quality & Stability Improvements 2024.5.v13
notes.content:
Hi all!

We just released a series of updates addressing some of your initial feedback of the first few days of the 2024 combat playtest. 

A few of these changes should make especially the duel more engaging and fun to play, so we're curious to hear what its effect is! There are also improvements to the physics look & feel, accessibility and general stability.

What's New

 You can now knock out opponents even if their helmet absorbed the blow - hits negated by armour do concussion damage
 You can now also toggle thrusts with `LMB` + tap  `Ctrl` 
 AIs can now use thrusting attacks
 Added a debug settings menu, where you can try out a number of settings making characters more or less rigid.
 Melee camera sensitivity now scales with how far your arm is dragged out. You can tweak the sensitivity's min (at or towards the center) and max (out away from the center) in the `Gameplay` settings


Improved

 Improved physics balance & rigidity, characters should now have more swing in their arms, but with a stable root and less wobble
 Tweaked weapon & damage model to make armour a bit less OP. Swords will now more often confer blunt damage through mail and helmets, and the strongest cuts even penetrate mail at times
 You now should be able to reposition your arm more precisely without triggering attacks when you don't want to
 Improved AI distancing and aggression, they should close the distance better and pose more of a challenge


Fixes and minor changes

 Fixed bug where character's hair would disappear when sprinting
 Fixed not being able to equip bow
 Fixed a Settings bug that led to (hidden) physics settings not always initializing correctly
 Fixed some clipping issues with the Bozen great helmet
 Tweaked concussion damage, requiring stronger hits to deliver knock out blows
 You now hear maille rustling when attacking
 A couple more bugfixes


Thanks everyone for your feedback so far, it's been immensely helpful in pinpointing the biggest issues and making these improvements!

notes.title: Regular Update 2023.4.v48
notes.content:
Collision VFX
This update includes a dynamic vfx system for collisions. When objects impact each other or slide across the ground, these collisions are accompanied by dust effects. This feature has been in the works for some time and they add a lot to the physicality, so we're very happy to have this in the game! This VFX system will be expanded to include blood effects in a future update.

Try using World Interaction Mode [L Alt] to throw around and drag some objects, and see how they react to the environment.

Dynamic Conflicts
We improved the system that generates dynamic conflicts between parties in the world. Every entity in the world belongs to a party, and whenever some hostile world action occurs between party members, these parties will enter into conflict with each other, creating possibility for emergent campaign gameplay. If a party is already in conflict, they will join the opposing side. 

You can try this out in the demo by spawning a new party [End] (they will be neutral by default). If you then lure an enemy into attacking them (by positioning yourself such that a neutral party member is between you and the enemy), the neutral party will be drawn into this conflict on your side! For now, they will permanently remain friendly.

AI
The AI has been improved to work with the increased range of possibilities of conflicts. They will now seek new targets if an opponent is far, dead or unconscious, and have snappier movement when in combat. 

Changes & Improvements

 Weather will be randomized when loading the game mode for the first time
 Characters have a chance of dropping their weapons on death
 Improved death procedure to show more of the animation
 Increased probability of farmers spawning with tools
 Spawned farmer parties now spawn with tools that have collision
 Improved physics smoothness, characters now are a bit less springy and move more smoothly when perturbed
 Improved AI performance when spawning in many parties
 Improved settings menu spacing & key rebind screen
 Increased pitch to make sword clangs sound more like swords
 Updated some UI assets to reflect new styling



Fixes

 Fixed crash that could occur whilst reloading the game mode
 Fixed loading screen getting stuck whilst reloading game mode
 Fixed bug that caused 2H weapons to spawn in incorrectly
 (Mostly) fixed characters going nekkid when they died
 Fixed bug that didn't show tooltips in in-game Pause & Settings menu
